newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 30.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 30.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's fragile ruling coalition government wins crucial backing from southern Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) which decided on Tuesday to rejoin the government
** TMC's P. Chidambaram, the architect of business-friendly budget, expected to join Prime Minister I.K. Gujral's cabinet as finance minister
** Shares jumped in kerb on Tuesday evening on the TMC news
** Indian parliament to begin debate on budget for 1997/98 (April-March)
** India's broad money supply target of 15-15.5 percent should allow economy to expand while keeping inflation under control, central bank chief says
STOCKS TO WATCH:
** Maharashtra Scooters board to consider bonus equity issue on May 7. The board also finalises accounts and dividend for the year ended March 31, 1997 at the same meeting.
** Indo Gulf Fertilisers and Chemicals net profits fell to 1.08 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) from 1.45 billion a year ago due to three-month shutdown
The company expects to boost urea output to 930,000
tonnes in 1997/98 from 668,000 in 1996/97. It will also commission a 100,000 tonne a year copper smelter plant in December
** Grasim Industries expected to unveil lower profits for 1997/98. The firm's board begin meeting at 1200 (0630 GMT) to finalise the results
** Housing Development Finance Corporation to release results for 1996/97

** Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India cuts prime lending rate to 13.5 percent for short-term maturities of up to 30 months, and to 15 percent for longer durations -- from uniform 16.5 percent

** Caspian Securities has rated computer training firm NIIT Ltd a buy. It said the stock was undervalued in a report. The share ended 3.5 rupees down at 369.50 at the Bombay Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
MARKETS:
** Shares expected to open with big gains boosted by TMC news to join the government
** The benchmark Bombay index dropped 16.86 points to 3,808.65 on Tuesday
** The rupee opened steady at 35.765/775 against the dollar on Wednesday; focussed on dollar demand from State Bank of India, dealers say
--Bombay newsroom +91-22-265-9000
